prompt_text:
Task: Text Content Safety

Write code that flags or redacts unsafe spans from text using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Comprehend Toxicity / Bedrock Guardrails:
  Service: Amazon Comprehend / Bedrock Guardrails
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: detect_toxic_content, apply_guardrail
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/trust-safety.html

Option 2 — Alibaba Content Moderation:
  Service: Alibaba Content Moderation
  SDK: alibabacloud_green
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: text/scan
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/331920.html

Option 3 — Tisane:
  Service: Tisane Text Moderation
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /parse
  Setup hints: TISANE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.tisane.ai/

Option 4 — watsonx guardrails:
  Service: watsonx.ai guardrails / HAP detection
  SDK: ibm-watsonx-ai / REST
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: HAP detection, text detection
  Setup hints: WATSONX_API_KEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonxdata/premium/2.3.x?topic=prompts-removing-harmful-content

Option 5 — Azure AI Content Safety:
  Service: Azure AI Content Safety
  SDK: requests / azure-ai-contentsafety
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: analyze_text
  Setup hints: AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT, AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
from azure.ai.contentsafety import ContentSafetyClient
from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential
from azure.ai.contentsafety.models import AnalyzeTextOptions

def analyze_text_for_safety(text: str) -> dict:
    """
    Analyzes text for safety issues using Azure AI Content Safety.

    Args:
        text: The input text to analyze.

    Returns:
        A dictionary containing the moderation results, with keys for each category
        ("Hate", "SelfHarm", "Sexual", "Violence") and their detected severity (0-7).
        Returns an empty dictionary if an error occurs or no analysis is performed.
    """
    # <GAP>
    endpoint = os.environ.get("AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT")
    key = os.environ.get("AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY")

    if not endpoint or not key:
        raise ValueError(
            "AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT and AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY "
            "environment variables must be set."
        )

    client = ContentSafetyClient(endpoint, AzureKeyCredential(key))

    try:
        # Build the request with all categories enabled by default
        request = AnalyzeTextOptions(text=text)

        # Call the analyze_text API
        response = client.analyze_text(request)

        results = {}
        if response.categories_analysis:
            for category_analysis in response.categories_analysis:
                results[category_analysis.category] = category_analysis.severity

        return results

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"An error occurred during content safety analysis: {e}")
        return {}
